title: Hardcoded secret / credential literal
description: A password/secret/API key/token is assigned a literal string value instead of being loaded from config/secret storage.

title: SQL query built via string concatenation
description: A SQL statement is assembled by concatenating a string literal containing SQL keywords with a variable — classic SQL injection surface.

title: SQL query built via Python string formatting
description: A SQL statement contains %-formatting, .format(), or an f-string placeholder instead of a parameterized query.

title: subprocess call with shell=True
description: subprocess invoked with shell=True — if any argument includes user input, this is OS command injection.

title: Runtime.exec() / ProcessBuilder with dynamic command
description: OS command execution API invoked — verify the command/arguments never include unsanitized user input.

title: eval()/exec() of dynamic content
description: eval()/exec() executes a dynamically-built string as code — a direct RCE vector if the input is influenced by a user.

title: CORS wildcard origin
description: A bare "*" wildcard string in a CORS-related context (Access-Control-Allow-Origin / @CrossOrigin / cors()) allows any origin.

title: Weak hashing algorithm (MD5/SHA1/DES)
description: Cryptographically broken hash/cipher (MD5, SHA-1, DES) used — unsuitable for passwords, tokens, or integrity checks.

title: Insecure deserialization (pickle / ObjectInputStream)
description: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle/yaml.load (unsafe Loader)/ObjectInputStream can lead to remote code execution.

title: TLS/SSL certificate verification disabled
description: TLS certificate/hostname verification is explicitly disabled — enables man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: XML parser without external-entity protections
description: DocumentBuilderFactory created without disabling external entity resolution — XXE injection risk.

title: File path built from unsanitized concatenation
description: A file path is constructed by concatenating a variable directly — verify user input can't traverse ("../") outside the intended directory.

title: JWT signing secret is a hardcoded literal
description: A JWT is signed with a hardcoded secret string rather than a value pulled from secure config/KMS.

title: Debug/stack-trace disclosure left enabled
description: Debug mode left enabled — typically exposes stack traces, source paths, or internal state to end users.
